decisions.reason: The peak-alignment decision does not change the second V hierarchy. The source message's separate second-V refinement is already captured by a complete same-message MODIFY.
The source changes the positional alignment of the Hero V and accent peaks, while the accent's literal derivation and exact geometry-match rules remain valid unchanged.
The source establishes a shared horizontal peak relationship but does not necessarily modify any aspect of the approved Hero V geometry.
Peak alignment is a compositional positioning rule and does not alter the existing shared terminal shape, intent, constraints, or evaluation rule.
Neither the Hero V–accent peak alignment nor the separate second-V height instruction changes the required geometry or architectural treatment of the E and L forms.
The source's second-V clause changes its vertical hierarchy, not its glyph derivation or right-arm geometry; that hierarchy is owned by a separate Requirement.
The peak-alignment refinement does not change the wordmark's kerning or unified-reading requirement.
The geometric peak-alignment decision has no entailed effect on the deferred champagne material treatment.
The client notes that the annotations are useful but does not change the requirement to provide design rationale with review rounds.
The source contains no decision about attachment formats or Mac-viewable proofs.
